 95| def _parse_line_with_peaks(rline: str) -> Tuple[List[float], List[float], str]:
 96|     """Parse a line containing peaks consisting of mz and intensity values with optional comments.
 97| 
 98|     Args:
 99|         rline (str): Line with peaks read from the MSP.
100| 
101|     Returns:
102|         Tuple[List[float], List[float], str]: mz, intensity and peak comments obtained from the line.
103|     """
104|     comment, rline = get_peak_comment(rline)
105|     mz, intensities = get_peak_values(rline)
106| 
107|     return mz, intensities, comment
108|

110| def get_peak_values(peak: str) -> Tuple[List[float], List[float]]:
111|     """Get the m/z and intensity value from the line containing the peak information."""
112|     tokens = re.findall(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?)", peak)
113|     if len(tokens) % 2 != 0:
114|         raise RuntimeError("Wrong peak format detected!")
115| 
116|     tokens = list(map(float, tokens))
117|     mz = tokens[0::2]
118|     intensities = tokens[1::2]
119|     return mz, intensities
120|

122| def get_peak_comment(rline: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
123|     """Get the peak comment from the line containing the peak information."""
124|     try:
125|         comment = re.findall(r"[\"\'](.*)[\"\']", rline)[0]
126|         rline = rline[: rline.index('"')]
127|     except IndexError:
128|         comment = None
129|     return comment, rline

132| def parse_metadata(rline: str, params: dict):
133|     """Reads metadata contained in line into params dict.
134| 
135|     The complexity of this function stems from the fact that MSP allows for many different formats of metadata.
136| 
137|     Parameters
138|     ----------
139|     rline: str
140|         The line of the read MSP file that contains metadata.
141|     params : dict
142|         The params that the key value pairs of the metadata line will be added to.
143|     """
144|     splitted_line = rline.split(":", 1)
145|     if len(splitted_line) != 2:
146|         return
147| 
148|     key, value = splitted_line[0].strip().lower(), splitted_line[1].strip()
149| 
150|     if key == "comments" and "=" in value:
151|         _parse_comments(value, params)
152|     elif key == "synon" and rline.count(":") >= 2:
153|         _parse_synon(rline, params)
154|     else:
155|         # Fallback for generic key: value pairs
156|         params[key] = value
157|

159| def _parse_comments(value: str, params: dict):
160|     """Parses key-value pairs from comments line into params."""
161|     value = value.replace("'", '"')  # Normalize quotes
162|     pattern = (
163|         r'(\S+)="([^"]*)"|'
164|         r'"(\w+)=([^"]*)"|'
165|         r'"([^"]*)=([^"]*)"|'
166|         r"(\S+)=(\d+(?:\.\d*)?)"
167|     )
168|     for match in re.findall(pattern, value):
169|         match = [i for i in match if i]
170|         if len(match) == 2:
171|             m_key, m_value = match
172|             m_key = m_key.strip().lower()
173|             m_value = m_value.strip()
174|             if m_key == "smiles" and m_key in params:
175|                 params[f"{m_key}_2"] = m_value
176|             else:
177|                 params[m_key] = m_value
178| 
179| 
180| def _parse_synon(rline: str, params: dict):
181|     """Parses synon lines with multiple colons."""
182|     parts = rline.split(":", 2)
183|     synon_key = f"{parts[0].strip().lower()}: {parts[1].strip().lower()}"
184|     synon_value = parts[2].strip().replace(",", ".")
185|     if synon_key == "synon: metb n":
186|         params.setdefault(synon_key, []).append(synon_value)
187|     else:
188|         params[synon_key] = synon_value
189|

191| def contains_metadata(rline: str) -> bool:
192|     """Check if line contains Spectrum metadata."""
193|     has_colon = ":" in rline
194|     return has_colon and not _is_golm_peak_format(rline)

197| def _is_golm_peak_format(rline: str) -> bool:
198|     """This function detects whether a line is a line containing peaks in the GOLM MSP format.
199| 
200|     The GOLM MSP format encodes peaks as mz:intensity - this resembles a metadata line, but actually contains peaks.
201|     It is therefore necessary to explicitly check this corner case when determining whether a line is peaks or metadata.
202| 
203|     Args:
204|         rline (str): Line to check whether it contains peaks from GOLM
205| 
206|     Returns:
207|         bool: Whether the line is a line with peaks from GOLM or not.
208|     """
209|     return re.match(r"(\d+:{1}\d+)", rline) is not None
